stories.headline: Super Micro guides FY2027 revenue to $65B-$72B after $60B in Q4 orders; margins nearly double

key_facts.fact: Super Micro reported fiscal Q4 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) net sales of $11.1 billion, versus $10.2 billion in Q3'26 and $5.8 billion in Q4'25, and below the Wall Street consensus of about $11.6 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Net sales of $11.1 billion versus $10.2 billion in Q3'26 and $5.8 billion in Q4'25.

key_facts.fact: Gross margin jumped to 17.5% from 9.9% in the prior quarter and 9.5% a year earlier; quarterly net income was $1.178 billion versus $195 million in Q4'25, and non-GAAP EPS was $1.70.
key_facts.excerpt: Gross margin of 17.5% versus 9.9% in Q3'26 and 9.5% in Q4'25. Net income of $1,178 million versus $483 million in Q3'26 and $195 million in Q4'25.

key_facts.fact: The company guided fiscal 2027 revenue to $65 billion-$72 billion, against an analyst consensus of roughly $53-54 billion, and Q1 FY2027 revenue to $14.5 billion-$15.5 billion versus about $11.7 billion expected.
key_facts.excerpt: For the full fiscal year 2027, the company expects revenue of $65 billion to $72 billion, compared with an analyst consensus of $54.4 billion, according to Bloomberg.

key_facts.fact: Supermicro said it took in more than $60 billion of new orders during fiscal Q4 alone, taking backlog to a record entering fiscal 2027; full-year FY2026 revenue was $39.1 billion, up from $22.0 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Fiscal 2026 revenue nearly doubled to $39.1 billion, while Supermicro received more than $60 billion in new Q4 orders and entered fiscal 2027 with record backlog.

key_facts.fact: CEO Charles Liang attributed the revenue shortfall to short-term customer delays tied to power shortages, cooling and networking readiness, calling it 'purely a timing story'.
key_facts.excerpt: While Q4 revenue came in at $11.1 billion due to some short-term customer delay in power shortage, cooling, and networking. We know this is purely a timing story.

key_facts.fact: SMCI shares rose roughly 7%-10% in extended trading after the Tuesday-evening report.
key_facts.excerpt: The company surprisingly missed expectations on revenue, but the big beat on its bottom line, combined with strong guidance for the current quarter, helped its stock gain more than 7% in extended trading.

stories.headline: Foxconn posts record Q2 profit as AI servers pass half of revenue for the first time

key_facts.fact: Hon Hai (Foxconn) reported second-quarter net profit of NT$59.97 billion (about $1.86 billion), up 35% year-over-year and its highest ever for a second quarter, beating an LSEG consensus of NT$58.8 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Net profit for the April to June period for Nvidia's biggest server maker and Apple's top iPhone assembler was T$59.97 billion ($1.86 billion), versus an LSEG consensus estimate of T$58.8 billion.

key_facts.fact: Consolidated sales reached NT$2.53 trillion (about $78.6 billion), up 41% year-over-year and 19% from the prior quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: In the second quarter, Hon Hai generated NT$2.53 trillion in consolidated sales, up 41 percent from a year earlier and up 19 percent from a quarter earlier.

key_facts.fact: The cloud and networking division, which builds AI servers, accounted for 51% of revenue, up from 48% in Q1 and above 50% for the first time; smart consumer electronics (including iPhones) fell to 29%.
key_facts.excerpt: The cloud and networking division accounted for 51 percent of second-quarter total revenue, up from 48 percent in the first quarter, while the smart consumer electronics division made up 29 percent.

key_facts.fact: Operating profit hit an all-time quarterly high of NT$94.8 billion, up 68% year-over-year, with operating margin at 3.75%; EPS was NT$4.27.
key_facts.excerpt: operating profit of NT$94.8 billion (approx. $2.9 billion) ... operating profit also reaching an all-time quarterly high, surging 68% year-over-year.

key_facts.fact: On the earnings call, Foxconn said July revenue set an all-time monthly record of NT$946.5 billion, up 54.2% year-over-year, raised its 2026 capex growth forecast to over 30%, and said next-generation Vera Rubin AI racks begin shipping in the fourth quarter.
key_facts.excerpt: July revenue surged to NT$946.5 billion (approx. $29.4 billion), setting an all-time monthly high, up 54.2% year-over-year... CEO Jiang Ji-Heng revealed that the next-generation AI rack (Vera Rubin) will begin shipping in the fourth quarter, with an ASIC market share target of over 40%.

stories.headline: Nebius AI cloud revenue jumps 514% to $575M; ARR hits $3B and capex guidance stays at $20B-$25B

key_facts.fact: Nebius Group reported Q2 2026 group revenue of $582.3 million, up 454% year-over-year, with AI cloud revenue of $574.9 million, up 514%; annualized run-rate revenue reached $3.0 billion at the end of June, up 56% from $1.9 billion in March.
key_facts.excerpt: Q2 group revenue of $582.3 million, was up 454% year-over-year. Nebius AI cloud revenue grew 514% year over-year to $575 million, ARR reached $3.0 billion.

key_facts.fact: Group adjusted EBITDA was $236 million, versus a $21 million loss a year earlier, lifting the group margin to 41% from 32% in Q1; the Nebius AI segment ran at a 50% adjusted EBITDA margin.
key_facts.excerpt: Group adjusted EBITDA reached $236 million, compared with a $21 million loss last year, while its margin rose to 41% from 32% in the first quarter.

key_facts.fact: The company reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance: revenue of $3 billion-$3.4 billion, year-end ARR of $7 billion-$9 billion, ~40% adjusted EBITDA margin and capital expenditures of $20 billion-$25 billion. Q2 capex alone was about $5.7 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Growth requires substantial funding, with Q2 capital expenditures of approximately $5.7 billion and full-year 2026 CapEx guidance of $20 billion–$25 billion.

key_facts.fact: Nebius closed four AI cloud deals in the quarter with an average total contract value above $1 billion each, and said total contract value grew nearly fourfold from the prior quarter; the stock rose about 12% in premarket trading.
key_facts.excerpt: helping it close four AI cloud deals with an average total contract value exceeding $1 billion each. Total contract value grew nearly fourfold from the previous quarter.

key_facts.fact: Nebius said it expects over $9 billion in customer prepayments during 2026 and that it again sold out of capacity as fast as it was brought online.
key_facts.excerpt: We expect over $9 billion in customer prepayments in 2026. We are reaffirming our full-year 2026 guidance across all metrics.

stories.headline: Google cuts Pixel 11 Pro RAM to 12GB and raises prices $100, blaming a 'severe' RAM shortage

key_facts.fact: Every Pixel 11 model launched on August 12 starts $100 above the equivalent Pixel 10, and the Pixel Watch 5 costs $50 more than the previous model: Pixel 11 at $899, Pixel 11 Pro at $1,099, Pixel 11 Pro XL at $1,299, Pixel 11 Pro Fold at $1,899 and Pixel Watch 5 at $399.
key_facts.excerpt: The Pixel 11 phones that were just introduced today all start at $100 more than the equivalent Pixel 10 devices. The Pixel Watch 5 costs $50 more than the last model too.

key_facts.fact: Google reduced RAM in the base Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL to 12GB, down from 16GB in the equivalent Pixel 9 and Pixel 10 devices; 16GB is now a paid upgrade.
key_facts.excerpt: Google has actually reduced the amount of RAM in the base versions of the Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL. Those have 12GB of RAM, compared with 16GB of RAM in the equivalent 9- and 10-series devices.

key_facts.fact: A Google spokesperson said the industry is 'navigating a severe, supplier-driven RAM shortage' and that Google had to adjust both Pixel 11 pricing and RAM configurations to mitigate it.
key_facts.excerpt: The tech industry is navigating a severe, supplier-driven RAM shortage and we will need to adjust Pixel 11 pricing and RAM configurations to mitigate this while delivering maximum value for our customers.

key_facts.fact: Google said it is compensating with software and silicon optimization, claiming the new Pro models will be faster than last year's comparable 256GB SKUs despite the lower memory.
key_facts.excerpt: through software and silicon optimization, you can expect faster and smoother performance from this year's Pro models when compared to last year's comparable 256GB SSD SKUs.

key_facts.fact: The price and spec changes are a direct consumer-facing consequence of AI data-center buildouts absorbing memory supply, a market where DRAM contract prices surged sharply and HBM suppliers are fully allocated.
key_facts.excerpt: A key reason that RAM, storage and chips are far more expensive than they were a year ago is that AI companies are buying up as much of those components as they can to build out their data centers.

stories.headline: Korea signs power pacts for its chip megaclusters: 6GW+ for Honam by 2029, 14GW+ for Yongin by 2041

key_facts.fact: On August 12 the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment, the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City, Samsung Electronics, SK hynix and state utility KEPCO signed three power-supply agreements at KEPCO's Gyeongin Construction Headquarters in Seoul.
key_facts.excerpt: The ministry, the Jeonnam–Gwangju Integrated Special City, Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, and Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO) took part in the signing.

key_facts.fact: The southwestern Honam semiconductor complex will get roughly 3GW of power in a first phase so its earliest fabs can start operating in 2029, with cumulative capacity later expanding beyond 6GW.
key_facts.excerpt: The southwestern Honam semiconductor complex will initially receive about 3 gigawatts of power to support the start of fab operations in 2029, with capacity later expanding to more than 6 GW.

key_facts.fact: The two Yongin complexes, anchored by Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, are expected to need more than 14GW of electricity by 2041, delivered in phases as transmission lines and generation come online.
key_facts.excerpt: Two semiconductor complexes in Yongin, Gyeonggi Province, are expected to require more than 14 GW by 2041, with electricity to be supplied in phases.

key_facts.fact: Initial Yongin supply through 2032 will come from three 1GW LNG plants built inside the national complex — using replacement quotas from retiring coal plants — plus short-distance transmission lines; longer term the grid will be extended to East Coast and central generation.
key_facts.excerpt: In the first stage, by 2032, short-distance lines near the complex and three 1 GW LNG power plants within the complex will be built using replacement quotas for aging coal plants to meet initial demand.

key_facts.fact: Part of the private-sector share of first-phase Honam grid costs may be covered by national fiscal support under Korea's Special Act on Semiconductors, which took effect on August 11.
key_facts.excerpt: financial support from the national budget will be sought through inter-ministerial consultation in line with the 'Semiconductor Special Act,' which came into effect on August 11.

key_facts.fact: Climate and Energy Minister Kim Sung-hwan said speed of power supply is what will determine the success or failure of the semiconductor megaprojects, which were announced on June 29 as part of Korea's 'Three Major Megaprojects'.
key_facts.excerpt: "The key factor that will determine the success or failure of the semiconductor megaprojects is speedy power supply."
